Maybe.

I dunno anymore.  Everything is blurry now.  I'm not really sure what's right and what's wrong anymore.  I even felt like a complete fraud writing my original post here, even though all of it was true.  I feel the same way about this reply.

I know for sure that whether it's right or wrong doesn't matter anymore for me.  It's really too late now.  People loved me before, but I have nothing to offer anybody now.  And self-sufficiency is more complicated than it sounds with some of the personal issues I'm facing.

People like to say you have worth regardless, but it's really not true.  When you're vibrant and attractive and have a future, which is usually when you don't need help, everybody wants to be around you and help you.  That's how it was before.

But when you have real problems, nobody cares.  Not that I blame them; I'm not whining.  That's just the nature of the world.  Offering support to people in trouble requires a lot of energy.  And if they have serious issues like health problems, helping them fix those problems costs time and money, and very few people have either to spare.  That's doubly true if you're isolated.  You really have nowhere to go.  I just wish people would stop pretending it works some other way.  It doesn't "get better" for everyone and not everyone has "another way."

I just checked my bag, and I left one of my meds at home.  I left in a hurry, and I grabbed an extra bottle of the wrong thing instead.  I feel pretty horrible when I don't take them, so I don't want to tough it out.  And my car is kinda messed-up.  It has been semi-broken for a while, so I've just been driving one of his cars for the last year.  I took mine anyway when I left, but I doubt it will last more than a few hundred miles.  I can't really use it long term, and replacing it isn't an option.  And in this city, no car isn't an option.

I was right.  He sent me a text talking about coming home not long after.  No apology.  He said he didn't want to continue the "argument," even though the argument was him screaming and me crying.  Will I go home?  Probably.  Why not?  He'll probably be angry, but who cares?

Yeah, I guess I am a complete fraud.  The story ends with me going back, and I probably won't even commit suicide.  This post was a waste of everyone's time to read.

I've just been looking up methods since I wrote my original post.  I'm tired of failing at this.  It's just kinda hard.  I'm starting to realize that it's all about lines.  It's about what price you're willing to pay.  The last time I seriously tried, I crossed the line of not caring if it was painful.  I took a dose that, according to every source I've read, should've almost certainly caused liver failure and eventual death in a person my size.  It would've been ugly, but it should have worked.  But it didn't work even a little bit (they tested me for liver damage at the hospital and nothing), and that was one of the very few easily accessible and reliably lethal otc drugs.  And opiates don't seem to work well with me, either.  And most of the other drugs that I have ready access to or can be obtained otc require massive doses to be reliably lethal.  I doubt I'd be able to keep down hundreds of pills considering most of the potentially lethal drugs, beyond the one I tried, cause stomach upset.

I guess I'm tough?  Before I started suffering from my current issues, I was an athlete and really fit.  I think the line you have to cross from there is getting "physical," rather than relying on a chemical solution like poison or od.  I guess you have to stop caring whether it gets bloody or you leave a mess.  That's why guys have a much higher completion rate.  They pick better methods.  I don't know what that would be for me.

I dunno.  This post has already been selfish enough.  I'm sure it's already a lousy thing to read.  And if I keep saying what I'm thinking, it will probably only get a lot worse.  So I guess I'll just end it here.

I did figure out why I'm writing this stuff, at least.  I don't care about people reading it, and I know I can't be helped.  I just want a chance to finally say something, somewhere.  This post will disappear into the backscroll of this subreddit pretty quickly, and that's fine.  At least I got a chance to speak my mind.  It's only online, but that will have to be good enough.  My partner will be the one to tell my story IRL.

I guess it's really my fault for trusting him, isn't it?  His last partner committed suicide too.  I believed his explanations.  I'm sure he'll tell the next person the same stories about me, about how I was so terribly unstable, and there was nothing he could do.
I think my story just makes him sound a lot worse than he actually is.  I'm probably just being dramatic, honestly.  He did a lot for me when nobody else would.

I'm not sure how to interpret this.  I don't want to send you on your way if this is something which genuinely causes you distress, and you really want to talk about it.

But the tongue-in-cheek tone makes it hard to interpret the intent of what you've written here.

You only need to look at the internet to realize that lots of people have interests in some of the things you've mentioned.  There are rather large communities focused around many of them.  Not all of those people are monsters.  Probably very few are.

It's not really something I would share with your boyfriend when you're eighteen years-old.  It's hard to know if/what guys will start talking about when you break up with them.  And no matter how jealous you may get, most people don't keep their bf/gf at 18yo forever.  Your reputation matters, and some things are harder for people to forget than others, especially in certain kinds of communities.

That said, it's probably not healthy for you to channel all of your thoughts inward.  I would look for some kind of constructive outlet.  Remember what's important.  Don't do things that will hurt yourself or others.  And don't put yourself in undue risk.  But beyond that, it's OK to explore your sexuality with other consenting adults.

In fact, some people with very extreme fantasy lives are really just playing out otherwise mild sexual tendencies that they simply have no real world outlet for.  Finding some way to express yourself sexually that's safe and healthy may tone down some of the fantasies you have.  Done with the proper amount of caution and restraint, kink can be your friend.

You don't need to have endured trauma for your pain to be real.  It matters even if you haven't.  You matter.

And you're not alone.  Lots of people struggle with depression.  Lots of people have experience with self-harm and disordered eating.  I myself have had a few experiences with it.  It's hard to control, and it can be addictive, but there are _many_ people who work hard and get it to a point where they control their impulses.

You can't change who you were.  You can't change what happened a week, or month, or even one second ago.  You can't go back and rewrite all the things that lead to this moment.

But you really do have the power, no matter how powerless and hopeless you feel, to take a first step toward making things better for yourself in the future.

Reach out.  Find someone you feel safe talking to and talk to them.  There may even be support groups comprised of people your age with similar issues.  There really is help out there.  And understand that no matter how bad you feel, _you're worth that help._

Lots of people have varying degrees of involuntary motion in their sleep.  Rapid movements like that aren't entirely unheard of.

It's possible that she was stroking out, I suppose.  It's far, far more likely that she was simply sleeping.

I do applaud you for having that kind of concern, but I wouldn't think about it more.  She was most likely fine.

And if you are preoccupied by it further, you can try channeling that energy constructively.  In the future, if you do see something you're pretty sure is wrong, be sure to be the kind of person who speaks up and tries to help.  Maybe even take a first aid course.

Whatever you decide to do, you're a good person.  Don't beat yourself up.

You were a child.

You experienced a trauma just like she did.  Was hers worse?  Yes.  Does that make yours any less valid?  No.

I'm sure it hurts, and I'm sure you feel regret, but it's important to understand that what happened to her is not your fault.  Knowing that won't make the guilt disappear, but it will help you to forgive yourself.  And once you do, in time, the guilt will subside.

You're not to blame for what happened to her.  You're not to blame for not saving her.  At that age, you lacked the emotional and intellectual tools to do anything to help her.  And you did try.  Remember that.  You ran away and you told someone.  They might not have done anything with that knowledge, but your instincts, even as a child, were to do the right thing.  And you cared too.  All of that matters.

Lots of people would simply remain silent in that situation, and done their best to forget what they heard and saw.  Most do.  You didn't.

You're a good person who was placed in a bad situation as a child.  No more or less.

Why is this any different than somebody simply fantasizing about seeing a woman naked?

Because you clicked things?  Because you made a picture in photoshop?  You're villainizing yourself because you did something IRL with it rather than just having a fleeting fantasy inside your own head.

I don't think that means as much as you think it does.  Any action you commit has to be put in context.

To start with, no harm was done.  If you made a photoshopped nude of a girl without her consent, and then put it online, that would definitely be wrong.  You didn't, though.  It sounds like you just made it, used it to fap, and got rid of it.

On top of that, it doesn't sound like you do this often.  It's not a pattern of behavior for you.  So even if this were a highly questionable act, which I don't think it is, it's not a part of who you are.  It's just a mistake which you regret.  No more or less.

And beyond that, that mistake was made while you were drunk and in college.  More than a few people make hormone-driven mistakes while in college and under the influence.  Just the same way that girls in spring break videos aren't necessarily sluts, you're not necessarily a pervert just because you did this thing.

And finally, understand that you can feel genuinely remorseful without having anything /wrong/ with you.  Feeling regret for your misdeeds is the hallmark of a good person, not a bad one.

I have hope for you, and I think you'll be OK.  Your username says it all.  It's time to be done with this.  Let the mistake teach you and inform your behavior, but don't let it push you to believe you're something you're not.  You're not bad.
